title: Pursue Your Light
dateline: A street west of the platforms.
mood: Guinevere wakes in a street she never fell into, while Angela holds a bell of pink light against the dark.

hero.alt: Guinevere on her feet in a ruined street, blood at her lip and her pink hair blowing, one of her drones at her hand.
hero.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana interactive drama

segs.t: White light went over the roofs, and the stone under Guinevere’s cheek shook.
She opened her eyes.
Stone, and a low wall an arm’s length away. Dust was coming down on her sleeve.
The last thing she remembered was the gap under the platforms, and Vexana small in the white above it. Here there was only the wall, and no sound behind it.
She got up on her knees. One drone circled her, slow. The other hung low at her shoulder, its eye dark.
Over the top of the wall rose two shoulders of purple plate edged in gold. They did not move.
She climbed over the wall into the road. Nobody was in it.
A stripe of the road had melted to glass. It ran straight across the stones and stopped at the wall.
A machine knelt there with its back to the wall. Its eyes were dark, and so was the heart-shaped crest on its chest. The chest plate had split down the middle, and the edges were bent outward.
As if someone climbed out of it.
She half remembered white. A back between her and the glare, and metal shrieking. Then dark. She could not tell if she had dreamed it.
At the end of the road a stair climbed to the platforms. Above them the clouds had torn wide open, and light fell through the hole.
In it stood the Mother Matrix, whole now. Its violet eyes were turned down at the platforms. The white she had woken to was fading from its chest.
Up on the platform, something small lay where the light had struck.
It moved. It got a staff under itself and rose to one knee.
At Guinevere’s collar the star blazed hot.
Vexana.
She took one step toward the stair.
It shot at her. She isn’t one of them.

media.alt: On the scorched platform among the ruins, Vexana gets her staff under her and rises to one knee.

segs.t: Light began to gather again in its chest.
She opened her wings. They came thin and flickering, and they held.
Enders were dropping off the Matrix’s wings. They came down on the head of the stair and filled the air over the gap, more every moment.
Not through that,
she thought.
Not on wings like these.
Below, along the waterfront, a glow of pink light stood against the seawall at the foot of the gap. Gray shapes clung all over it.
From below, then,
she thought.
Up the gap from the water.
“Guinevere!” Layla’s voice cracked over the channel. “Guinevere! Report!”
“Coming,” said Guinevere.
She left the dead machine where it knelt and flew low for the water.
A ruined waterfront under the Singularity.
Angela held the shield out with both hands. It stood around the four of them on the broken seawall, a bell of pink light.
Enders pressed on it from every side. They came down the seawall and up out of the bay. Each blow rang through her arms, and each one cost her a little.
Tetra rode at her shoulder. Its camera eye turned with the fight.
“I’ve locked on to the enemies!” Layla stood on a slab of seawall in the middle, the cannon on her shoulder. “Ruby, left. Fanny, high.”

media.alt: Four girls stand on a ruined waterfront below a vast four-pointed tear of violet light in the sky; then Fanny and Layla take aim side by side, blade and cannon ready.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana interactive drama

segs.t: Angela opened a pane in the shield. Layla’s shot went through it. Angela closed it before the next claw fell.
Ruby’s scythe went through the next pane before anyone asked. Fanny’s blades went through the one after.
“Funny in the head,” Layla muttered at Ruby and Angela, lining up again. “Both of you. The pane’s open before I ask.”
“Thank you!” said Angela.
Layla fired instead of answering.
The Enders had closed a ring on them at the seawall, and it was still closing.
Shield load rising,
her systems told her. She knew.
The ring packed in tighter. Claws scraped down the pink light. It dimmed where they dug in.
Angela set her feet. “I won’t let anyone hurt my friends!”
She pushed. The shield swelled and threw the nearest Enders back across the stones.
Her ears caught a hum far off over the water. One drone. The other was silent.
A gold streak came low across the water. The Enders on the shield turned and swarmed at it. Angela opened a pane, reached out, and caught a wrist.
She pulled. Guinevere came through on her knees and skidded across the stones.
Her cheek was cut. One arm guard was cracked. One drone hung low, its eye dark. From the cracked guard a little black-haired doll swung on its clip.
“Vexana’s up there.” She was gasping. “It’s going to fire on her again. They’ve packed the gap, and my wings won’t push through.”
“The traitor?” said Layla.
The pink light shivered under Angela’s hands.
Guinevere’s chin came up. “Her name is Vexana.”
Then she gave them what she had, fast. “I fell into the gap. I woke up three streets away. I don’t know how.”
She took a breath. “A machine took the Matrix’s shot for me. Purple and gold. It’s kneeling against a wall, cracked open from the inside.”
She looked at Layla.
“Someone climbed out of it.”
Layla’s cannon dipped a hand’s width. “The commander saw it on the feed. She said get to you if we could.” She looked at the gray ring. “We couldn’t.”
Fanny looked at the cracked arm guard. She said nothing. Her blades stayed up.
Angela had a pane open before Ruby moved. Ruby swung the scythe once through it, and lightning crawled down the blade. The ring on the platform side split apart and fell into the water.
“We escaped from this cage,” Ruby said, with a look at Angela. “We can also destroy it!”

media.alt: Ruby, her scythe raised, shouts at the Enders, while behind her Angela holds the shield open with light in both hands.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana interactive drama

segs.t: Angela looked at the star blazing at Guinevere’s collar.
At the long table, in the weeks of the search, she had put down her spoon. “I came back once. People come back.”
She had meant the avenue. The dark, and a child crying somewhere in it. Androids lying around her in the smoke, every one with her face. They had come to fire on this city, and so had she.
Ruby’s ragged breath, and the red in Ruby’s eye. She had called Ruby’s name, and the red had gone out.
“I thought I’d killed you,” Ruby had said.
“I came back.”
All through the search that star had stayed lit. “It only says yes,” Ruby had said, the morning they made it a tracker.
“Then yes is something,” Angela had said.
Ruby stood at her side now, sparks still running off the scythe. Her eye was blue.
People come back,
she thought.
Angela looked up from the star, into Guinevere’s face.
“Go, Guinevere, pursue your light.”

media.alt: Angela holds out both hands, pink light glowing in her palms, her small drone Tetra floating above her.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana interactive drama

segs.t: She opened a pane on the platform side, wide enough for one. Wind came in off the bay, cold with salt.
Guinevere looked at her for one breath. Then she went through.
As she passed, the dark ring in her low drone lit yellow. The drone rose until it hung level with its twin.
Angela closed the pane behind her.

Both drones went ahead of Guinevere into the gray over the gap. It broke apart in front of them, and her streak climbed through, red-gold. Ahead of it, over the platforms, the great chest was nearly full of light.
